title: Review: Kc calculations and Q; IUPAC nomenclature; Homologous series
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: OR02#t1 term and clue written for the game; OR03#t3 term and clue written for the game; OR03#t2 term and clue written for the game; OR02#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EQ03#N.8, OR02#N.9, OR03#N.10, EQ03#N.6a, OR02#N.5, OR03#N.7, EQ03#N.14a, OR02#N.4, OR03#N.4, OR02#N.7, OR03#N.11. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Homologous series
items.clue: A family of compounds in which each member differs from the next by CH₂.

items.label: Prefix
items.clue: Part of a name for a side group, such as methyl, ethyl, chloro or bromo.

items.label: Suffix
items.clue: The ending of a name that shows the main group: -ol, -al, -one, -oic acid.

items.label: General formula
items.clue: A single algebraic expression that fits every member of a family of compounds.

questions.stem: 0.400 mol SO₂ and 0.200 mol O₂ are sealed in a 2.00 dm³ vessel. At equilibrium the vessel contains 0.300 mol SO₃. What is Kc for 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g)?
Butane, C₄H₁₀, boils at −1 °C and is sold as camping gas. Dodecane, C₁₂H₂₆, boils at 216 °C and is a liquid in diesel fuel. Which explains the difference?

options.text: Dodecane molecules contain more C–C and C–H bonds, which must break before it can boil.
Dodecane molecules contain more hydrogen atoms, so they form more hydrogen bonds.
Butane and dodecane belong to different homologous series, so their properties differ.
Dodecane chains are longer, so the induced dipole–dipole forces are stronger.

questions.explanation: Longer chains have more electrons and more contact, so the forces between molecules are stronger. More energy is needed to separate them.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH(CH₃)CH₃?
questions.explanation: Six-carbon chain. From the left, the C=O is on C3 (from the right, C4) and the methyl on C5.

questions.stem: N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g). N₂O₄ is placed in a sealed vessel at an initial concentration of 0.200 mol dm⁻³ and the mixture is allowed to reach equilibrium at constant temperature. At equilibrium, [NO₂] = 0.080 mol dm⁻³. What is the value of Kc at this temperature?
questions.explanation: 0.080 of NO₂ uses 0.040 of N₂O₄, so [N₂O₄] = 0.160 mol dm⁻³. Kc = 0.080² ÷ 0.160 = 0.040 mol dm⁻³.

questions.stem: Alcohols have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH. What is the molecular formula of the alcohol with seven carbon atoms?
What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CHO?
questions.explanation: Four-carbon chain including the –CHO carbon, which is C1. The methyl is on C2.

questions.stem: Back to the sealed flask: H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g). It was filled with 0.500 mol H₂ and 0.500 mol I₂ and no HI, in a 2.00 dm³ flask. It has now reached equilibrium and holds 0.800 mol HI. What is Kc at this temperature?
questions.explanation: 0.800 mol HI uses 0.400 mol each of H₂ and I₂, leaving 0.100 mol each. Kc = 0.800² ÷ (0.100 × 0.100) = 64. Two terms on top, two below: the volume and the units cancel.

questions.stem: Which pair of compounds are successive members of the same homologous series?
questions.explanation: Both are carboxylic acids (CₙH₂ₙO₂) and they differ by one CH₂: ethanoic acid and propanoic acid.

questions.stem: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₂Cl?
questions.explanation: Longest chain four carbons. Numbering from the CH₂Cl end gives {1, 2}, lower than {3, 4}. Prefixes alphabetical.

questions.stem: The boiling points of four successive alcohols are: methanol 65 °C, ethanol 78 °C, propan-1-ol 97 °C and butan-1-ol 118 °C. Which statement explains this trend?

options.text: Longer molecules have more H atoms, so they form more hydrogen bonds.
Longer molecules contain more covalent bonds to break on boiling.
Heavier molecules need more energy to move, whatever the forces.
Induced dipole–dipole forces grow with chain length; each has one –OH.

questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonding per molecule stays about the same. Each extra CH₂ adds electrons and contact area, so the induced dipole–dipole forces grow.
pent: five-carbon chain. -2-one: C=O on C2. 3-methyl: a CH₃ branch on C3.
